description: Issue summary: Customer BrightAnswers reports recurring elevated 5xx rates on their dedicated tenant during mixed workload periods (chat + embedding uploads). Errors surface as short 1–3 minute waves multiple times per hour.
impact: Multiple production endpoints for BrightAnswers saw ~12-18% 5xx for short windows, causing higher latency and client-side retries. Customer reports downstream throttling and some failed long-running websocket sessions.
environment_notes: Dedicated cluster in us-west region. Tenant pinned to redwood-13b-v2 for chat routes and open-research-7b-quant for nightly embedding jobs. Observed during business hours and during scheduled bulk embedding uploads.
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Customer issues high-concurrency websocket streaming sessions (keepalive enabled) to chat route.
2) Concurrently upload a large embedding batch (multipart) to embeddings route.
3) Monitor accept-queue depth on ephemeral proxies and api-gateway metrics (accept.queue_length, ephemeral_proxy_gc_cycles).
4) Observe elevated 5xx and runtime preemption logs when GC window aligns with incoming handshake bursts.
logs:
[2026-03-12T14:03:21Z] apigw: accept_queue=128 -> drop_rate=0.12, upstream=ephemeral-proxy-7 status=502
[2026-03-12T14:03:22Z] proxy: gc_cycle_start pid=2173 retained_fds=104
[2026-03-12T14:03:23Z] runtime: preempting-model-worker worker_id=42 reason=socket-half-open
[2026-03-12T14:03:24Z] runtime: OOM-avoid-reclaim triggered; restart-signal sent to worker
[2026-03-12T14:03:25Z] apigw: upstream_reset count=9 route=/v1/chat streaming=true
investigation_notes:
- Initial hypothesis: accept-queue pressure + ephemeral-proxy GC windowing is causing a burst of half-open sockets which escalate to the serving runtime preempting workers and triggering GPU reclaim attempts.
- Correlated apigw accept_queue spikes with proxy GC traces; GC cycles frequently align with incoming websocket handshakes during embedding upload contention.
- Observed that when GC cycles start, FD handoff latency increases ~4–8x leading to HTTP/2 stream resets and upstream restart loops.
- Heap and file descriptor stats from ephemeral-proxy show transient FD exhaustion during GC windows (avg open fds jump ~200).
- No immediate kernel-level OOMs; issue appears to be resource fragmentation and timing amplification across proxies and runtime watcher logic.
temporary_workaround:
1) Temporarily throttle BrightAnswers embedding upload concurrency (request rate limit) and stagger uploads; recommended client-side backoff.
2) Increase ephemeral-proxy keepalive timeout to reduce socket churn during GC windows.
3) Apply rate limit on websocket handshake concurrency per-tenant in apigw as immediate mitigation.
resolution_plan:
Short term: deploy a hotfix to apigw that adds handshake-sidecar backpressure when downstream accept_queue exceeds threshold (canary to 10% of traffic in us-west).
Medium term: update ephemeral-proxy GC to perform incremental GC with smoother FD reclamation and emit early load signals to apigw.
Long term: refactor runtime preemption logic to avoid GPU reclaim on transient half-open socket bursts and improve keepalive pooling semantics for mixed embed/chat workloads.
postmortem_actions:
- Owner: Runtime reliability team to implement preemption safety gate (ticket INT-2034).
- Proxy team to add incremental GC prototype and run load tests (PR submitted).
- DevX to update customer quickstart recommendations for embedding + streaming concurrency.
- Create synthetic test that reproduces GC-window handshake collision for future regression testing.
resolution: In progress: Canary patch to apigw backpressure deployed 2026-03-14 to 10% of us-west traffic. Early telemetry shows 70% reduction in 5xx wave amplitude for canary customers. Full rollout pending additional proxy GC mitigations and runtime safety checks.
comments: 2026-03-12 Priya Nair (Support): Customer BrightAnswers opened a ticket after seeing repeated 5xx spikes. Provided initial logs and sample request IDs. Escalating to runtime and proxy teams.
2026-03-12 Marcus Lee (SRE): Observed accept_queue spikes aligning with reported windows. Captured ephemeral-proxy traces and initial heap/fd stats. Marked as potential resource-churn amplification.
2026-03-13 Anika Patel (Proxy Eng): Found that proxy GC bursts were full-stop cycles; incremental GC branch reduces peak fd reclamation. Preparing a diff for testing.

2026-03-13 Liam O'Connor (Runtime Eng): Runtime preemption logic currently treats repeated half-open sockets as indication of runaway worker; adding debounce to prevent immediate GPU reclaim. Working on linked internal ticket INT-2034.

2026-03-14 BrightAnswers Support Contact (Emily Zhang): Confirmed that after temporary concurrency limits and staggered uploads, immediate user visible errors dropped. Awaiting permanent fix timeline.
2026-03-14 Priya Nair (Support): Deployed apigw handshake backpressure canary. Monitoring dashboards; will update SLA status and customer communication.
